definition: In information science and information retrieval, relevance denotes how well a retrieved document or set of documents meets the information need of the user.
details: Relevance may include concerns such as timeliness, authority or novelty of the result.
story: Think of a referee whose job is to be completely honest about who touched the ball last. Before trusting a machine, someone has to measure how good it really is — fairly and honestly. It is the exam that separates “it sounds good” from “it actually is good”. What gets measured is what actually gets better. That shared ruler is Relevance (information retrieval).
